newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 11.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:

* The Federal Trade Commission said it will seek a federal court injunction to block Staples' $4 billion acquisition of Office Depot because the merger would violate antitrust law and lead to higher prices.
* Newmont Mining won its bid to acquire Santa Fe Pacific Gold in a stock deal valued at $2.46 billion, and Santa Fe agreed to pay Homestake Mining $65 million to end their merger agreement.
* Boeing is negotiating to have Delta buy all its future jetliners from Boeing, and people familiar with the matter say a pact could be similar to the one between Boeing and AMR's American Airlines.
* Niagara Mohawk Power agreed to pay $4 billion to 19 power producers to change or end agreements requiring the firm to buy electricity for above-market prices.
* The Dow industrials rose 78.50 to 7,079.39 points. Bonds were unchanged and the dollar dropped.

* Television broadcasters and three direct-broadcast satellite firms tentatively agreed to end a fight involving satellite customers who illegally receive network programs from distant cities by cancellng illegal access the programs.
* Insurance broker Johnson & Higgins is considering either going public or selling itself for what some analysts believe could be at least $1 billion.
* GE agreed to buy two companies that service aircraft engines, Greenwich Air and UNC Inc, for $875 million in cash and stock plus debt assumption.
* Boeing said it has formed a trading venture with Berkshire Hathaway Inc unit FlightSafety, entering into the broader jet-pilot training business.
* IBM, Oracle, Netscape and Sun Microsystems announced an agreement to make their software products work together.
* Chubb has an agreement in pricinple to sell its real estate unit for about $1 billion to a private company run by the chairman of Patriot American Hospitality, people familiar with the deal say.
* Palomar Medical said the Food and Drug Administration cleared its Epilaser system for removing body hair, but a unit of MEHL/Biophile International sued Palomar for patent infringement.
* Four Japanese fund firms suspended business with Nomura Securities after Nomura said its executives directed company money to a client.
* The breakneck expansion of the credit-card business has spelled record profits and soaring stock prices for banks that concentrate on issuing credit cards, known as monoline issuers.

But now intense competition, slowing growth and shrinking profit margins are prompting some of those same companies - whose appeal to investors until lately has been as pure credit-card plays - to branch out. --Heard on the Street.

* Investors have a new worry on their hands as states and cities across the country increasingly turn to a controversial type of municpal bond to shore up their beleaguered public pension-fund systems. --Credit Markets.
